answer: A cedar bond registry blocks fakes. Each applicant bonds one device key, and verifiers match the key against a work record, with mismatch forfeiting the bond. For k identities the total is k squared units, so the k-th identity adds 2k minus 1 units, cost grows quadratically with n, fees cannot be pooled because payments trace to one operator, the registry enforces the fee, and failure loses the bond. One fake costs 1 unit; 1,000 fakes cost 1,000,000 units. A rented yarrow record fails on key mismatch; an honest agent pays once and keeps the echo of work as reputation.
